rooms.name: Spring Porch
rooms.description: Three streams meet at different heights. Each tastes of a different part of the mountain.

encounters.cue: Compare the lips of the three spouts.
encounters.result: Each has a different notch filed in it. A keeper filling cups by lamplight could identify a spring by the shape of its stream.

rooms.name: Copper Spring
rooms.description: A copper-coloured film shivers on the water. A scratched arrow points upstream against the flow.

encounters.cue: Look at the film beside the scratched arrow.
encounters.result: It breaks around a tiny upwelling. The arrow marks where to dip a sample before the bright surface closes again.

rooms.name: Milk Spring
rooms.description: White mineral dust makes this stream look like milk until it settles in a still cup.

encounters.cue: Inspect the pale rings in a still cup.
encounters.result: The rings stop at three pencilled lines. A keeper timed the settling dust by watching the lines come into view.

rooms.name: Night Spring
rooms.description: The third stream is so dark it shows the ceiling stars at midday. It runs colder than the other two.

encounters.cue: Shield the surface of the dark spring from the light.
encounters.result: The stars disappear below a cupped hand. They are pale grains in the ceiling reflected in water clear beneath its dark surface.

rooms.name: Mixing Bowl
rooms.description: Mineral lines trace the three streams where they mix without touching for a whole arm's length.

encounters.cue: Trace the mineral lines to where they join.
encounters.result: All three bend at a little chip in the stone. The first rough edge, rather than the narrowest point, starts the mixing.

rooms.name: Sluice Model
rooms.description: A child's miniature waterworks sends half its flow around a buried stone and back through the same arch.

encounters.cue: Look beneath the miniature buried stone.
encounters.result: The child used the domed end of a broken cup. Its handle makes a little tunnel the water can find for itself.

rooms.name: Survey Table
rooms.description: A wax tablet pairs the copper spring head with the return pressure. Its final column names the scale on the salt siding.

encounters.cue: Compare the wax survey with the water marks on the table leg.
encounters.result: The return needs two heads of spring pressure against the rail trim. The listening works valve can divide the flow without draining the ferry.

rooms.name: Plumb Well
rooms.description: The plumb line slowly spins. A notch in the rim records where the spin stops when the lake is low.

encounters.cue: Inspect the edges of the notch in the well rim.
encounters.result: It is wider than the line by exactly one cord twist. The surveyor allowed the weight to settle before calling a reading.

rooms.name: Tea Ledge
rooms.description: Surveyors steeped their tea in the warm spring. Three rings from their cups still darken the ledge.

encounters.cue: Compare the rings on the tea ledge.
encounters.result: One ring has a gap the size of a chipped lip. The same chipped cup was set down at every survey.

rooms.name: Limestone Ear
rooms.description: A curl of limestone catches a distant voice from the listening works and brings it close enough to whisper.

encounters.cue: Feel the ridges inside the limestone curl.
encounters.result: One ridge is polished at the height of a seated ear. A listener once waited here long enough to wear a shine into stone.

rooms.name: Siphon Crown
rooms.description: The pipe rises and turns back on itself. At its highest point a bead of water remains suspended in cloudy glass.

encounters.cue: Look at the bead in the crown glass.
encounters.result: A hair is sealed across the glass just behind the bead. From either side a surveyor could sight along the same level.

rooms.name: Sample Steps
rooms.description: Nim keeps a stoppered sample from each year's first flood, even the year the city insists was dry.

encounters.cue: Nim the surveyor rinses every cup twice. She distrusts a drawing until she has drunk the water.
encounters.result: Nim keeps both the original survey and fresh measurements on the survey table. The old return joins the bitter spring before it reaches the borough.

rooms.name: Minnow Lens
rooms.description: A convex pool makes tiny fish look the size of trout. The fish shelter above a warm leak in the return pipe.

encounters.cue: Look where the minnows gather above the pipe.
encounters.result: The fish face a steady plume of bubbles. When one leaves, the others close up exactly over the warm seam.

rooms.name: Dry Cascade
rooms.description: A polished waterfall hangs without water. The highest ledge lines up with the old evacuation shelf.

encounters.cue: Inspect the back of the highest dry lip.
encounters.result: A spoon-shaped hollow shelters dry grit. The old current once fell cleanly over the lip without wetting the rock behind it.

rooms.name: Chalk Compass
rooms.description: A compass drawn on the floor points toward the dam hinge instead of north.

encounters.cue: Inspect the pinhole at the centre of the chalk compass.
encounters.result: A length of fine thread is caught in the hole. The surveyor swung the arc around a pin before ruling the line to the hinge.

rooms.name: Flow Orchard
rooms.description: Dwarf willows take up minerals from the spring. Their pale leaves turn green nearest the working bypass.

encounters.cue: Read the tags tied low on the willows.
encounters.result: They carry planting dates and the colour of the first leaf. The same tree could serve as a flow record for years.

rooms.name: Glass Float
rooms.description: A sealed glass float hangs in a vertical tube. A little bell silences it when the flow is even.

encounters.cue: Examine the bell at the float's resting height.
encounters.result: A felt collar catches the bell rim at the centre mark. An even flow is the one reading the keeper can recognise by silence.

rooms.name: Underbridge
rooms.description: The undersides of the bridge stones bear the masons' names and the widths of their shoulders.

encounters.cue: Compare the shoulder marks beneath the stones.
encounters.result: The narrowest mark lies under the last stone. The builders picked someone who could still squeeze out after setting it.

rooms.name: Hinge Trail
rooms.description: The path runs over flat-worn bolt heads. Each bolt ties the spring gallery to the dam.

encounters.cue: Inspect the sides of a flat-worn bolt.
encounters.result: A pair of deep spanner bites survives below the walking surface. The trail became a footpath only after the gallery was bolted fast.

rooms.name: Headwater Shrine
rooms.description: Travellers leave three cups here, one full, one empty and one with room for another sip.

encounters.cue: Turn the three cups to catch their maker marks.
encounters.result: All bear the same thumbprint. The potter made the offering as a set, with room for the drinker to decide the last share.
